questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Mendel's law of independent assortment implies that
options: alleles segregate independent of one another during gamete formation.
traits are encoded by independent genes.
alleles segregate independent of their location on the chromosome during gamete formation.
traits are always encoded by different chromosomes.
questions.solution:
Mendel's law of independent assortment states that when two pairs of traits are combined in a hybrid, the segregation of one pair of characters is independent of the other pair of characters.

This implies that the alleles of different genes segregate independently of one another during gamete formation. The allele a gamete receives for one gene does not influence the allele received for another gene.

Answer: alleles segregate independent of one another during gamete formation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In a haplodiploid ant species, sons are haploid and produced from unfertilized eggs, while daughters are diploid and produced from fertilized eggs. A single queen establishes a colony after mating with three different unrelated males. The queen uses the sperm from all three males equally to produce her female offspring. The average genetic relatedness between two randomly selected female offspring in this colony will be:
questions.solution:
In a haplodiploid system, females are diploid, receiving half of their genes from the mother (queen) and half from the father (male). Males are haploid, meaning all sperm produced by a single male are genetically identical.

The genetic relatedness between two full sisters (sharing the same father) is $0.75$. This is because they share $100\%$ of their paternal genes ($0.5 \times 1 = 0.5$) and $50\%$ of their maternal genes ($0.5 \times 0.5 = 0.25$), giving $0.5 + 0.25 = 0.75$.

The genetic relatedness between two half-sisters (having different fathers) is $0.25$. They share $0\%$ of their paternal genes (since the males are unrelated) and $50\%$ of their maternal genes, giving $0 + 0.25 = 0.25$.

Since the queen mates with $3$ males and uses their sperm equally, the probability that two randomly selected daughters share the same father is $\dfrac{1}{3}$, and the probability that they have different fathers is $\dfrac{2}{3}$.

The average genetic relatedness ($r_{avg}$) is the weighted average of these probabilities:

$r_{avg} = \left(\dfrac{1}{3} \times 0.75\right) + \left(\dfrac{2}{3} \times 0.25\right)$

$r_{avg} = 0.25 + \dfrac{0.50}{3}$

$r_{avg} = 0.25 + 0.1667 = 0.4167$

Rounding to three decimal places, the average genetic relatedness is $0.417$.

Answer: $0.417$

Genotype of Indian breed is $(B B D D Z z)$ and Australian breed is $(b b D D Z z)$ where gene $B$ and $D$ are linked genes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: If a female, who is a carrier of the haemophilia gene, has a child with a male who does not have haemophilia, which of the following predictions would be correct?
options: All the sons and none of the daughters will have haemophilia.
All daughters and none of the sons will have haemophilia.
$50 \%$ of the sons and $50 \%$ of the daughters will have haemophilia.
$50 \%$ of the sons and none of the daughters will have haemophilia.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The pathway that determines skin pigmentation in dogs is governed by two unlinked genes ( $\mathbf{I}$ and II). While gene $\mathbf{I}$ determines the type of pigment, gene II is responsible for its deposition in skin cells. Allele $\mathbf{P}$ (gene I) results in a black pigment; whereas, p produces a brown pigment. While allele $\mathbf{Q}$ (gene II) results in the deposition of pigment, $\mathbf{q}$ will not allow the same. Alleles $\mathbf{P}$ and $\mathbf{Q}$ are dominant over $\mathbf{p}$ and $\mathbf{q}$, respectively. Lack of pigment deposition results in an albino phenotype. When two canines with genotype PpQq are mated, the phenotypic ratios of offspring would be
options: 12(black):3(brown):1(albino)
9(black):3(brown):4(albino)
9 (black):7(albino)
12(black):4(brown)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The phenomenon of "linked genes" contradicts which of the following fundamental principles of genetics?
options: Law of segregation.
Principle of dominance and recessivity.
Principle of independent assortment.
Incomplete dominance.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
Birth records of 4 babies were mixed up in a hospital. The ABO blood groups of the four babies were known to be $\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}, \mathrm{AB}$ and O . To determine their respective parents, blood groups of all parents, except the father of baby III were tested. Choose the correct statements:
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline & \text{Blood Type} \\ \hline \text{Parents I} & \text{father} & \text{AB} \\ 2 - 3 & \text{mother} & \text{O} \\ \hline \text{Parents II} & \text{father} & \text{A} \\ 2 - 3 & \text{mother} & \text{O} \\ \hline \text{Parents III} & \text{father} & \text{Unknown} \\ 2 - 3 & \text{mother} & \text{A} \\ \hline \text{Parents IV} & \text{father} & \text{O} \\ 2 - 3 & \text{mother} & \text{O} \\ \hline\end{array}$
options: The blood group of the Father III could be A and baby III is A.
The blood group of Father III could be B and baby III is AB.
The blood group of Father III could be either AB or B .
The blood group of Father II could be O and baby III A.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
Seed traits of a given plant species following genetic inheritance are:
$\begin{aligned} \\ & \mathrm{S}=\text { long, } \mathrm{s}=\text { short; } \\ & \mathrm{W}=\text { wrinkled, } \mathrm{w}=\text { smooth; } \\ & \mathrm{Y}=\text { yellow, } \mathrm{y}=\text { white; } \\ & \mathrm{R}=\text { ribbed, } \mathrm{r}=\text { grooved } \\ \end{aligned}$

A cross was performed between two plants, $\mathbf{P}$ and $\mathbf{Q}$ of the same species; wherein, the plant $\mathbf{P}$ bears seeds that are homozygous recessive for grooved, homozygous dominant for long trait, and heterozygous for wrinkled texture and yellow colour. The plant $\mathbf{Q}$ bears seeds that are homozygous recessive for short and smooth traits, homozygous dominant for yellow colour and ribbed trait. Given that there are no influencing factors, state the resulting phenotype of the offspring for this cross.
options: The seeds of half the plants would be long, smooth, yellow and grooved
The seeds of half the plants would be long, wrinkled, white and ribbed
The seeds of all the plants would be long, wrinkled, yellow and ribbed
The seeds of half the plants would be long, wrinkled, yellow and ribbed

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In a long-term study of a population of a self-pollinated plant, it was observed that an allele, which significantly enhanced vegetative growth and production of flowers in the plant, did not expand in distribution over subsequent generations in the population. This could be because the allele is
options: dominant lethal in nature.
tightly linked to a gene that allows formation of large number of seeds in each plant.
linked to a gene that suppresses development of axillary branches.
tightly linked to a gene that suppresses development of pollen mother cells in the plant.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Huntington's disease is a genetic disorder that leads to defects in brain function and is always fatal. The affected gene consists of a sequence of DNA having multiple repeats of the nucleotide sequence CAG. A factor that determines whether an allele of this gene causes Huntington's disease or not is the number of CAG repeats. The graph on the right shows the age (in years) at which patients (each represented by a dot) first developed symptoms of Huntington's desease and the number of CAG repeats in the allele causing Huntington's disease in each patient. From the above graph, which of the following would be correct?
options: There could be factors other than number of CAG repeats that determine the age of onset.
There is a negative correlation between age of onset and number of CAG repeats.
Huntington's disease is fatal and is therefore not heritable.
Huntington's disease is heritable and can be passed onto offspring.
